:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.4.7`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noTopLevelLiterals`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule doesn't have a fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`json/top-level-interop`](https://github.com/eslint/json/blob/main/docs/rules/top-level-interop.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noTopLevelLiterals": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Require the JSON top-level value to be an array or object.

Modern JSON allows an object, array, string, number, boolean, or `null` at the top level.
Older parsers based on [RFC 4627](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4627) accept only
an object or array. Restricting the top level to those two forms improves compatibility and
leaves room to add more fields or items later.

## Examples

### Invalid

```json
"just a string"
```

### Valid

```json
{
  "property": "value",
  "otherProperty": 123
}
```

```json
["element", "anotherElement"]
```

```json

```

```json

```
